# Consumer tests

Read these rules before you write or register a consumer test. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="nr-49"></a>

## NR-49: Test the module formats consumers use `[GAP]`

> Consumer tests resolve the package in the module formats its consumers use.

Old number: 5.2.3.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: Delete hardhat/v2/plugin/test/node10-cjs-resolution.test.ts: `npm test` (node --test test/*.test.ts) still passes, and no check notices that no node10 trace remains. Fix: issue I-102.

Issues: I-102.

For each published payload a
fixture links, `test-consumer` resolves it by name in each module format the consumer uses and the payload exposes
([NR-60](../entries/NR-60.md)), and traces its declarations under `nodenext` when the conditions of [NR-50](../entries/NR-50.md) hold. A `nodenext` trace does not
prove a legacy mode: `node10` ignores `exports` and uses legacy package resolution, so substituting one for the other
proves a different package. Hardhat v2 consumers use `node10`. The isolated Hardhat v2 consumer has no `node10` proof:
the plugin's own test holds the only `node10` declaration trace ([NR-50](../entries/NR-50.md)), and `attw --pack` adds a static `node10`
verdict ([NR-51](../entries/NR-51.md)).

```jsonc
// ✅ Hardhat v2's TypeScript consumer profile. Under TypeScript 6, the plugin's test also sets
// "ignoreDeprecations": "6.0".
{ "module": "commonjs", "moduleResolution": "node10" }

// ❌ As proof of that profile: test-consumer's probe proves nodenext, not node10 (5.2.4).
{ "module": "nodenext", "moduleResolution": "nodenext" }
```

<a id="nr-50"></a>

## NR-50: Assert the resolved declaration file `[GAP]`

> A consumer test asserts the resolved declaration file, not merely successful compilation.

Old number: 5.2.4.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: Delete hardhat/v2/plugin/test/node10-cjs-resolution.test.ts: nothing fails. Fix: issue I-103.

Issues: I-103.

A consumer can
compile while TypeScript falls back to shipped source or resolves the payload's sources in the checkout instead of the
installed declarations. For each installed published payload that declares a root entry point and types, `test-consumer`
therefore runs `tsc --traceResolution` on a one-line import of the package, fails if that import does not compile, and
proves two things: the trace names a declaration the installed `package.json` declares (`types`, `typings` or a `types`
condition of `exports`), and no `.ts` module resolves from the payload's directory in the workspace. The probe resolves
under `nodenext`, whatever the consumer's own mode: a `.cts` file selects CommonJS and a `.mts` file ESM, once per
module format the consumer uses and the payload exposes. A consumer whose installation has no `typescript` skips the
probe. `test-consumer` compiles nothing else itself: any other compilation is the fixture's own `test` script's, and the
Hardhat v2 template's `hardhat test` does not type-check, so in `test-consumer` the probe is that consumer's only
declaration check. The probe does not trace a legacy mode such as `node10`: the option is deprecated from TypeScript 6
and its opt-out value differs per major, so no generic check can pin it. The Hardhat v2 plugin's own test traces
`node10` instead (`hardhat/v2/plugin/test/node10-cjs-resolution.test.ts`, run by `make test-hh-v2-plugin`), against its
symlinked `pkg/` rather than an isolated installation.

```text
✅ /tmp/fhevm-consumer-abc123/node_modules/@fhevm/hardhat-plugin/_types/index.d.ts
❌ /repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg/src/index.ts
❌ /tmp/fhevm-consumer-abc123/node_modules/@fhevm/hardhat-plugin/src/index.ts  (caught when the trace then names no declared file)
```

<a id="nr-51"></a>

## NR-51: Resolution checks supplement the consumer profile `[GAP]`

> Modern resolution checks supplement the real consumer profile.

Old number: 5.2.5.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: `git rm hardhat/v2/plugin/test/node10-cjs-resolution.test.ts`: every check and every test still passes, which is the rule's ❌ case 'no node10 trace anywhere'. Fix: issue I-104.

Issues: I-104.

`attw --pack` judges the packed types in every
mode the payload's module formats reach, and does not run for a Solidity-only payload ([NR-47](../entries/NR-47.md)); `test:consumer` adds
runtime execution and the package's actual supported toolchain. Neither substitutes its own convenient resolution mode
for the consumer contract. The declaration probe of `test-consumer` runs under `nodenext` ([NR-50](../entries/NR-50.md)) and adds to whatever
the fixture's own `test` script compiles; `test-consumer` compiles nothing else itself. A Hardhat v2 consumer's `node10`
resolution is traced by the plugin's own test, not by `test-consumer` ([NR-50](../entries/NR-50.md)).

```text
✅ attw --pack: static resolution matrix for the formats the payload ships
✅ test:consumer: supported toolchain, exact paths and runtime execution
✅ hardhat/v2/plugin's own test: node10 trace of the linked pkg/
❌ tsc under nodenext only, with no node10 trace anywhere: no proof that a Hardhat v2 consumer resolves the package
```

<a id="nr-54"></a>

## NR-54: Wrapping dev packages define test:consumer `[GAP]`

> Every dev package that wraps an npm-distributed package defines `test:consumer`.

Old number: 5.3.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Add a Makefile target or workflow step running `npm --prefix host-contracts-cleartext/v14 run test:consumer:dev`: no check fails. Fix: issue I-107.

Issues: I-02, I-107.

This is the stable public
command for proving the installed payload; optional stages share the stem (`test:consumer:run`, …) but callers invoke
only `test:consumer`. A mirror-only consumer project is already the consumer and is exempt.

The published entry's `consumerTests` is the SOLE registry of its consumer tests: per module format the payload exposes
(CJS, ESM, both for a dual package — derived from the published entry points), a non-empty array of manifest package
keys. Nothing registers a consumer by existing: a `test-consumer/<format>` directory beside the payload, a `test`
script, or a `file:` dependency on the payload carry no registration semantics. A format may register several suites,
and one consumer may be registered by several payloads. `test-consumer` lists, selects and runs exactly the consumers
this registry names, and `test-consumer-regenerate-package-lock` regenerates their lockfiles.

```text
✅ dual package: "consumerTests": { "cjs": [...], "esm": [...] }
✅ ESM-only package: "consumerTests": { "esm": [...] }
❌ dual package registering only "esm"
❌ an existing test-consumer/cjs directory with no registration
```

```jsonc
// ✅ The v3 plugin exposes ESM and registers two ESM suites: its fixture and the Hardhat template.
{
  "type": "esm",
  "consumerTests": {
    "esm": ["./hardhat/v3/plugin/test-consumer/esm", "./hardhat/v3/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg"]
  }
}

// ❌ A boolean waiver would remove consumer coverage instead of locating it.
{ "consumerTests": false }

// ❌ The single-string spelling is retired; a registration is always an array.
{ "consumerTests": { "cjs": "./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg" } }
```

A registered consumer must execute as the selected module format, define a non-empty `test` script, and directly link
the tested package through a directory `file:` dependency. An isolated (non-member) consumer is a `standalone` fixture
and carries a committed `package-lock.json`; a workspace-member consumer is an `internal-consumer` or a mirror-only
`published` template and carries none ([NR-64](../entries/NR-64.md)). A consumer that is not itself a payload sets `private: true`. The
validator checks all of these; `test-consumer` performs the isolated installation and execution, replaying the
committed lockfile where one exists.

```jsonc
// ✅ In the dev package that wraps ./pkg. One command owns the whole consumer test.
"scripts": { "test:consumer": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run --build-linked-dependencies" }

// ❌ A package-specific name cannot be discovered or invoked uniformly.
"scripts": { "test:hardhat-template": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run --build-linked-dependencies" }
```

## NR-56: Consumer tests run outside the workspace `[GAP]`

> A consumer test runs outside every workspace.

Old number: 5.3.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli test-consumer`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: resolveDestination() (test-consumer.ts:956) takes `--output` as given and assertSafeOutput() (:1005-1008) refuses only the filesystem root: `fhevm-npm test-consumer ./hardhat/v3/plugin --run --output ./hardhat/v3/plugin/test/consumer` installs and runs the consumer below the workspace root, where Node can walk up to the root's node_modules, and nothing fails. The same holds for a `test:consumer` script that adds `--output`, and for a TMPDIR that points inside the checkout. Fix: issue I-108.

Issues: I-01, I-108.

It creates a fresh temporary directory outside the checkout and
copies or generates the consumer there. A non-member nested below the workspace root is not isolated: Node can still
walk up to the root's `node_modules` and satisfy an undeclared dependency.

```text
✅ /tmp/fhevm-consumer-abc123
❌ /repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/test/consumer
```

## NR-57: Install candidates with --install-links `[HOLD]`

> Candidate directories are installed with `--install-links`.

Old number: 5.3.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli test-consumer`

The temporary manifest replaces each candidate
dependency with an absolute `file:` path to its `pkg/`; outside a workspace, npm packs such a directory and installs
the packed contents, exercising `files` and ignore rules without putting a `.tgz` in the dependency graph.

```jsonc
// ✅ Generated only in the temporary consumer; npm installs the packed directory contents.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:/repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg"

// ❌ A plain workspace version resolves to the workspace link, not the packed payload.
"@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "<N>.0"
```

## NR-58: Install a release set together `[GAP]`

> Packages released together are installed together.

Old number: 5.3.5.

Check: script.

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: The existing Forge fixture installs only forge-fhevm-std, while the release workflow set also contains the v3 plugin and current host contracts. No consumer installation includes all three, and resolveLinkedDependencies takes no release-set input. Adding an unrelated payload to the release set cannot make a consumer check require it. Fix: issue I-109.

Issues: I-109.

One clean install names every candidate in the release
set, so a local plugin cannot silently test against an older dependency fetched from npmjs.com.

```jsonc
// ✅ Both candidates are under test in the same dependency graph.
"devDependencies": {
  "@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:/repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg",
  "@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "file:/repo/host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg"
}

// ❌ The plugin candidate can resolve the host-contracts package from the registry.
"devDependencies": { "@fhevm/hardhat-plugin": "file:/repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg" }
```

<a id="nr-59"></a>

## NR-59: Prove a physical and isolated install `[HOLD]`

> The gate proves that installation is physical and isolated.

Old number: 5.3.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli test-consumer`

Issues: I-01.

Each candidate in `node_modules` must not be a
symlink, and its real path must stay below the temporary consumer. The test starts without the fixture's top-level
`node_modules` and without any installation root's lockfile. The only lockfile it can carry is the fixture's own
committed `package-lock.json`, which `test-consumer` replays with `npm ci --install-links`. A consumer that is a
workspace member has none, since its installation root locks it ([NR-64](../entries/NR-64.md)), and is resolved fresh with
`npm install --install-links`; so is an isolated fixture with no committed lockfile, which [NR-54](../entries/NR-54.md) already rejects, with a
warning that `--ci` turns into an error.

```text
✅ /tmp/fhevm-consumer-abc123/node_modules/@fhevm/hardhat-plugin
❌ /repo/hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg
```

<a id="nr-60"></a>

## NR-60: Resolve the package by name `[GAP]`

> The consumer exercises the published surface by package name.

Old number: 5.3.7.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli test-consumer`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: A valid bare main path ('index.js') is filtered by declaredEntryPoints; absent other prefixed entries, the runner incorrectly treats the package as having no root and skips name resolution entirely. Fix: issue I-110.

Issues: I-110.

For each published payload the fixture links
that declares a root entry point, `test-consumer` resolves the package name from the temporary consumer with the
consumer's own module system, `require.resolve` for CJS and `import.meta.resolve` for ESM, once per module format the
consumer uses and the payload exposes. It fails unless the resolved file lies inside the installed package and is an
entry point the installed `package.json` declares. It then traces the declarations by the same name ([NR-50](../entries/NR-50.md)) and, with
`--run`, runs the fixture's `test` script, the real consumer suite (`test:file` instead, with `--test-file`). A relative
import bypasses package resolution, so `test-consumer` resolves the name itself and does not rely on the fixture's
imports. A relative import into the checkout also fails when the temporary copy runs its suite ([NR-56](../entries/NR-56.md)).

```ts
require('@fhevm/hardhat-plugin'); // ✅ Exercises the installed manifest, exports and files.
require('../../plugin/pkg/src/index'); // ❌ Reaches source directly and proves nothing about the installed package.
```

<a id="nr-62"></a>

## NR-62: Run tests that share state one at a time `[GAP]`

> Consumer tests that share state outside their own process run one at a time.

Old number: 5.3.9.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: `fhevm-npm/base/checks/scripts.ts:773-778` requires `--test-concurrency=1` of every fixture that uses Node's test runner, even one whose tests share nothing; nothing checks whether a test shares state. Fix: drop that requirement (issue I-56). A test that shares state is caught in review.

Issues: I-56.

A test that talks to a
node, listens on a port or writes a shared file can collide with another: two senders race on one nonce, one test's
transactions change what another reads, two nodes claim one port. Distinct ports do not make such tests independent
when they still reach the same node or account. Tests on an in-process chain, such as Hardhat's in-process network
or forge's per-test EVM, share nothing and need no serial mode. `test-consumer` itself runs consumer packages and
fixtures one at a time.

```text
✅ forge test                       each test runs in its own in-memory EVM
✅ node --test src/*.test.js        each file creates its own in-process Hardhat network
❌ node --test src/*.test.js        every file sends to one `hardhat node` on localhost:8545, in parallel
```
